title: ClipSAT Course Schema (v2 — blocks model)
description: This top-level shape (a whole course: id + meta + chapters[]) is documentation/illustration ONLY — see the 'examples' block below for a full worked case. What's actually validated file-by-file (scripts/validate-content.js) is #/definitions/courseMeta against content/{track}/_meta.json, and #/definitions/chapter against each content/{track}/{chapter-slug}.json — one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so editing one chapter never requires touching or re-reading a file with every other chapter in it. NOT the format bank-data/*.json question banks use — those have their own ad hoc shape and are intentionally left alone. v2 replaces the original fixed definitions/theorems/keyFormulas/workedExamples split (v1, never adopted) with an ordered blocks[] model, after v1 was found not to match real chapter markup during the WP6 qudrat pilot — see docs/DECISIONS/0002-blocks-model-not-fixed-fields.md.

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the filename, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

chapters.description: Ordered list of chapters (topics) in this course.

practiceSet.description: Validates content/{track}/_practice-set.json — the track's numbered free-response practice list (the 'Practice set' section, distinct from bank-data/*.json's MCQ pools and from chapter content). NOT a blocks[]-shaped chapter: this is a flat, repeated list of {number, question, solution, difficulty} items. Two real 'variant' shapes exist (WP17 audit, appc): 'standard' (qud/tah/act2/est2/est) — .ph/.pn/.pq/.lvl {b|i|a}, shared toggleSol(this) JS, ~50 items, Basic/Intermediate/Advanced. 'compact' (appc) — .prow/.pn/.qt/.lvl (no b/i/a class suffix), an inline per-item toggle onclick instead of toggleSol(this), each item carries its own real DOM id, far fewer items, and a DIFFERENT difficulty vocabulary (Easy/Medium/Hard) — genuinely different real markup, not a normalization of the same thing. Optional per track — most tracks don't have this section yet.

variant.description: Selects which real markup shape to render. Absent/'standard' for the first five migrated tracks.

heading.description: The section's real <h2> text. Defaults to 'Practice set' (lowercase s) — set explicitly only when a track's real source differs, e.g. appc's real source capitalizes it 'Practice Set' (WP17).

icon.description: The section's real <span class="cn"> icon glyph. Defaults to '§' — set explicitly only when a track's real source differs, e.g. apbc's real source uses '⊘' with the heading 'Exam practice' (WP19).

introText.description:
The section's opening

, real per-track copy — a WP12 audit found practice-set.njk had been hardcoding qudrat's own wording (mentioning 'quantitative comparisons', a qudrat-only question type) for every track, live and wrong on the already-shipped tahsili page. Omit for a 'compact'-variant track whose real source has no intro paragraph (verify — don't assume).

id.description: 'compact' variant only — the item's real DOM id, e.g. 'appc-p1'.

difficulty.description: Free text, not a fixed enum — real source uses at least three different vocabularies (Basic/Intermediate/Advanced for most 'standard' tracks, Easy/Medium/Hard for 'compact', and — WP19, apbc — an item can be styled by one of Basic/Intermediate/Advanced's colors while its VISIBLE badge text is 'MCQ'/'FRQ', a different dimension entirely. This field always drives the CSS color class (must be exactly 'Basic'/'Intermediate'/'Advanced' for the 'standard' variant's color lookup to resolve); use levelLabel when the real visible text differs from this word.

levelLabel.description: Optional — the real visible text in the .lvl badge, when it differs from `difficulty` (e.g. apbc shows 'MCQ'/'FRQ' text on a Basic/Intermediate/Advanced-colored badge). Defaults to `difficulty` when absent.

courseMeta.description: Validates content/{track}/_meta.json — course-level metadata, kept separate from chapter files (one chapter per file, per docs/PHASE1-2_TARGET_ARCHITECTURE.md §2.2, so no single file needs the whole course read to edit one chapter).

id.description: Unique kebab-case course identifier matching the track slug, e.g. 'digital-sat'.

chapterOrder.description: Ordered list of chapter ids, e.g. ['qud-about', 'qud-arithmetic', ...]. The filesystem's directory listing order is NOT reliable display order — this is the explicit source of truth both the nav rail and the page's chapter sequence render from. Every id here must have a matching content/{track}/{id}.json file; scripts/validate-content.js checks this.

meta.description: Top-level course metadata displayed on the home card and course header.

title.description: Human-readable course title, e.g. 'Digital SAT Math'.

subtitle.description: Short tagline shown below the title.

prerequisites.description: List of course IDs that are recommended before this course.

color.description: Brand accent colour (hex or CSS variable) — see docs/DESIGN_TOKENS.md, prefer a var(--token).

icon.description: Optional emoji or short string used on the card badge.

estimatedHours.description: Approximate study hours for the full course.

examBoard.description: Awarding body, e.g. 'College Board', 'IB', 'Cambridge'. Proper noun, not translated.

officialLinks.description: External links to the exam board's own official portal/past-papers pages, shown on the track's Downloads section (downloads-block.njk). Track-specific real data — e.g. qudrat links to Qiyas and ETEC.

downloadsInfo.description: downloads-block.njk's copy. A WP12 audit found the template had been hardcoding generic English for every track — live and wrong on BOTH already-shipped qudrat and tahsili pages: the intro paragraph and PDF-card heading dropped each track's own name entirely, the PDF-card description silently swapped source's spelled-out 'eight' for a rendered '8', and the DOCX-card description was qudrat's own wording shown on tahsili's page too. Every text field here is a real per-track string, copied verbatim from source — never assume it matches another track's.

variant.description:
'ib' (ibsl, WP23) is a real structural deviation, not just copy: no self-serve PDF/DOCX export exists in source at all — the usual .dl-grid PDF/DOCX card row is replaced by a .formula-cards row of resourceCards[], led by an intro callout.note (introLabel) instead of a plain opening

, and the officialLinks past-papers widget nests INSIDE one specific resource card instead of sitting beside the PDF/DOCX cards. Absent/'standard' renders the original PDF+DOCX card shape every other track uses.

introText.description:
The section's opening

(standard variant) or the intro callout.note's body

(ib variant), e.g. 'Take the Qudrat material offline...'.

introLabel.description: 'ib' variant only — the intro callout.note's <span class="lab"> text, e.g. 'IB Mathematics SL — Key resources'.

pdfCardTitle.description: standard variant only. The PDF card's <h4>, e.g. 'Qudrat notes & practice'.

pdfCardDescription.description:
standard variant only. The PDF card's

. Source sometimes spells out numbers ('All eight chapters') rather than using a numeral — preserve exactly, don't substitute a count field.

docxCardLabel.description: standard variant only. The DOCX card's small <div class="di"> label. Defaults to 'DOCX · on request' (most tracks) — WP20 audit found appc/apstats' real source already says 'DOCX · Word equations' (live and wrong on both shipped pages) and act's says 'DOCX · editable'. Verify per track, don't assume the default.

docxCardTitle.description: standard variant only. The DOCX card's <h4>. Defaults to 'Native Word packet' — act's real source says 'Practice worksheet' instead, describing a genuinely different scope (the practice set only, not the whole chapter content).

docxCardDescription.description:
standard variant only. The DOCX card's

.

wide.description: Adds the 'wide' class (.fcard.wide) for a 2-column-span card.

body.description: Raw HTML allowed (matches source — e.g. inline <a> links, <code> tags).

officialLinksInside.description: Nest courseMeta.officialLinks[]'s '.dl.pp-card' widget as a child of THIS card's body (ibsl nests it inside its 'Mark Schemes' card) instead of the standard variant's placement as a sibling card.

resourceCards.description: 'ib' variant only — one entry per real .fcard in the .formula-cards row that replaces the PDF/DOCX cards.

worksheetLibraryText.description:
The Worksheet Library heading's

, includes the real worksheet count and whether it mentions Arabic (only true for tracks that actually have Arabic worksheets).

pageHeader.description: The <section class="subject-head"> at the top of the track page — page <h1> + a small stat row. Distinct from meta.title (used in <title>/nav/cards) since the on-page H1 can read differently.

eyebrowClass.description: Optional extra class on the eyebrow <span>, e.g. 'amber' — a real, functional CSS rule (.eyebrow.amber{color:var(--amber-text)}), not decorative-only. Only set when the track's real source has it (appc, WP17); omit otherwise.

testGenerator.description: Config for test-generator.njk. genFullExam(title, trackId, sections[], minutesArg) is existing engine.js JS. All copy fields are real per-track strings, not shared boilerplate — a WP12 audit found the template had been hardcoding qudrat's own copy for every track (a live bug on the already-shipped tahsili page: it showed 'Based on the Saudi GAT Qudrat exam'), and that a genuinely different track (act2) has its own intro paragraph, exam description, AND a button label that does NOT follow the 'Generate Full {examTitle}' pattern the other two tracks happen to share. Every field here must be copied verbatim from that track's real source, never assumed shared.

variant.description: appc's real source (WP17) differs from qud/tah/act2/est2/est in more than copy: the mini-test field wrapper is class="ctrl" not "tg-field", the Difficulty dropdown offers Easy/Medium/Hard (matching its practiceSet's 'compact' difficulty vocabulary) instead of Basic/Intermediate/Advanced with no 'selected' option and plain 'All' text instead of 'All levels', and the 'Show all answers' button carries an extra 'ghost' class and a data-state="hidden" attribute. 'compact' renders that real shape; absent/'standard' renders the original. 'ib' (ibsl, WP23) is a further real deviation: an outer <div class="testgen"> wrapper, mini-test buttons OUTSIDE .tg-controls, genTest(this, trackId) taking an explicit trackId argument (unlike standard/compact's genTest(this)), an intro callout.note (examIntroLabel) instead of a plain paragraph before the exam section, no .tg-divider, and — the real reason for the new variant — TWO 'Generate exam' buttons (one per IB course, AA/AI) instead of one, see exams[].

examTitle.description: Not translated — passed as a literal JS string argument to genFullExam(). For the 'ib' variant, unused directly (superseded by exams[]) but still populate with the first exam's real title to satisfy validation.

sections.description: Not translated — passed as literal JS string arguments. Shared across every entry in exams[] for the 'ib' variant (verified real source: ibsl's AA and AI exam buttons pass the identical sections array).

introText.description:
The first

under the 'Test generator' heading, above the mini-test controls. Not translated (no Arabic exists for this copy on any track checked). Optional — appc's real source has no intro paragraph at all here (verify per track, don't assume one exists).

examDescription.description:
The description

under 'Full official exam paper', above the generate button. Real per-track copy — do NOT assume it matches another track's wording or numbers.

examButtonLabel.description: The exam-generate button's exact visible text. Usually 'Generate Full {examTitle} ↻' but verify per track — act2's real source diverges from its own examTitle. For the 'ib' variant, unused directly (superseded by exams[].examButtonLabel) but still populate with the first exam's real label to satisfy validation.

examMinutesArg.description: The literal 4th argument passed to genFullExam() in source. A real source inconsistency: this is NOT always equal to the exam's stated duration in examDescription (qudrat/tahsili's source both pass 30 regardless of their own stated 52-min/50-min exams; act2's source passes 50). Preserve the real literal, don't derive it. Shared across exams[] for the 'ib' variant.

heading.description: The section's real <h2> text. Defaults to 'Test generator' (qud/tah/act2/est2/est all use this, lowercase g) — set explicitly only when a track's real source differs, e.g. appc's real source capitalizes it 'Test Generator' (WP17).

chapterQuizAfter.description: Some tracks' real source (appc, WP17) places a Chapter Quiz widget after the test-generator controls, identical in shape to a chapter's own quizWidget. Set true only when the real source has this; absent/false for the tracks that don't.

examIntroLabel.description: 'ib' variant only — the real <span class="lab"> text inside the callout.note that replaces the plain 'Full official exam paper' paragraph, e.g. 'Generate a full IB Math SL exam'.

exams.description: 'ib' variant only — one entry per real 'Generate exam' button (ibsl's real source has 2: AA and AI), each rendered with the SHARED sections[]/examMinutesArg above. Ignored by 'standard'/'compact'.

bilingualText.description: Every user-facing string in this schema uses this shape. 'ar': null means not yet translated — render English only, no Arabic toggle for this string. dir="rtl" is derived from the active language at render time, never stored here. HTML/LaTeX allowed inside (matches source markup — e.g. inline \( ... \) math, /, and occasional embedded ... for an Arabic term inside otherwise-English prose).

id.description: Unique slug within the course, e.g. 'qud-about'.

chapterNumber.description: The short badge shown next to the chapter title AND in the nav rail (source: <span class="cn">), e.g. 'i', '1', '5'. A string, not an int — some tracks use non-numeric badges.

railLabel.description: Optional — the nav rail's label for this chapter, if it differs from `title` (real source cases exist where the rail link has an Arabic translation but the chapter's own <h2> doesn't, or vice versa — don't assume they match, check both). Falls back to `title` if absent.

description.description: Optional one-line summary/tag line shown under the title.

chapterTag.description: Optional styled pill/category tag rendered right after the chead, before the first block. Track-specific (source class names like qud-tag/tah-tag/act-tag differ per track) and English-only in every real instance found (no track has ever translated it).

quizWidget.description: NOT quiz question data — every chapter's 'Chapter Quiz' section is a live widget (count/level selectors + a Generate button, genChapterQuiz() in engine.js) that pulls from bank-data/{track}.json at request time. This just tells the template whether to render that widget for this chapter.

chapterTag.description:
A small styled tag/breadcrumb line under the chapter heading. Two real variants exist in source, discriminated by 'variant': 'pill' (qud-tag/tah-tag — outer , track label + 1-2 small badge spans) and 'category' (act-tag — outer

, emoji + bold category name + a %-of-test badge + a middot-separated topic list). className/badgeClassName carry the real per-track CSS classes (e.g. 'qud-tag'/'qud-wt') so the partial never invents a class name.

badgeClassName.description: Small badge span's class, e.g. 'qud-wt', 'tah-wt', 'act-wt'. Required for 'category' variant's single weightBadge; for 'pill' variant it's the DEFAULT for any badges[] item that is a plain string — omit entirely when every badge supplies its own {text,className} (real case: ibsl-tag).

trackLabel.description: pill variant only, e.g. 'GAT Qudrat — Quantitative'.

oneOf.description: A badge with its OWN class, overriding badgeClassName — real case: ibsl-tag's 3 badges (P1 & P2 / AA SL / AI SL) each use a different class (ib-paper/ib-aa/ib-ai), not one shared class.

badges.description: pill variant only, 1-3 short badges, e.g. ['Ch.1 Arithmetic', 'No calculator']. Plain strings use badgeClassName; an {text,className} object overrides the class for that one badge.

emoji.description: category variant only, the leading emoji character.

category.description: category variant only, the bold category name.

topics.description: category variant only, middot-separated topic list.

chapterContent.description: All instructional material for a chapter, as an ORDERED sequence of blocks — order matters and is preserved from the source (unlike a v1-style split into separate definitions[]/theorems[]/etc. arrays, which loses document flow).

videos.description: Embedded topic videos (Appendix A benchmark task 6 — see docs/RECIPES.md #6).

provider.description: Extend this enum if a second provider is ever needed — don't add a differently-shaped field.

videoId.description: The provider's video ID (e.g. YouTube's 11-char ID), not a full URL.

topicTag.description: Optional free-text tag linking this video to a specific block by id.

block.description:
A discriminated union on 'kind'. Kinds were derived from what real chapter markup actually contains (grep counts across index.html as of WP6, docs/DECISIONS/0002): 'callout' covers definition/theorem/note/warning/proof/worked-example boxes (489+398 real instances — they all share one label+body shape, differing only in a style class), 'table' (22 instances, e.g. an exam section map), 'cards' (212 instances, e.g. a Format/Calculator/Skills/Signature stat grid), 'text' for a plain paragraph with no wrapper, 'explorer' (docs/DECISIONS/0003-explorer-block.md) for an interactive canvas widget — checked against 3 real instances (qudrat's qud-ratio ×2, qud-compare ×1), not guessed at — 'practiceProblem' (added WP12, act2) for the in-chapter
/

workedExampleCardBlock.description: A standalone <div class="fcard"> pairing a problem statement with its own solution (appc, WP17) — NOT part of a .formula-cards grid (cardsBlock), and structurally distinct from calloutBlock's 'example' style. label is the card's <div class="ft">, e.g. 'Worked Example 1.1' or 'Worked Example 2.3 — FRQ Style'.

problem.description: Rendered after a static, non-translated 'Problem.' bold prefix the partial emits — matches source exactly, don't duplicate the prefix inside this field.

practiceProblemBlock.description: The in-chapter <div class="problem"> pattern (act2, WP12): a question, a 'Show solution' toggle button (identical chevron-SVG markup and toggleSol(this) handler on every real instance — not parameterized here, the partial emits it verbatim), and a solution revealed on click. Distinct from calloutBlock (no style/label variants) and from the end-of-course practice-set's own numbered-problem shape.

explorerBlock.description: An interactive canvas widget — title bar, canvas, an accessible non-visual data-table fallback, 0+ sliders, 0+ live readout rows, an optional note. This is a REFERENCE + EXACT-SHELL block, not a generic reusable explorer type: canvasId/every control id/every readout id must match strings that public/js/engine.js's existing, per-explorer, hand-written JS already looks for — this schema does not invent new explorer behavior or let an author make up new ids. Its job is only to place the correct HTML shell (with those exact, pre-existing ids) at the right point in the chapter's reading order, and to hold the surrounding text bilingually. Verified against 3 real explorers (docs/DECISIONS/0003) — a genuinely different explorer shape (e.g. drag-based, multi-canvas) may need its own new block kind rather than being forced into this one.

title.description: The 'ex-top' title, e.g. '⊙ Explorer · Sharing in a ratio'.

canvasId.description: Exact id — must match what engine.js already wires up for this specific explorer. Required UNLESS canvas3d is set (a lazy-loaded 3D explorer has no plain <canvas> at all).

ariaLabel.description: The canvas's aria-label — a real, load-bearing accessibility field, not decorative. Ignored when canvas3d is set (canvas3d.ariaLabel is used instead).

canvas3d.description: Set ONLY for the lazy-loaded WebGL/Three.js 3D explorer shape (ibhl's cross-product explorer, calculus's later chapters — docs/DECISIONS/0011) — replaces the plain <canvas> with a '🧊 View ... in 3D' toggle button + an initially-hidden .ex-3d-wrap the 3D library renders into on click. The hint paragraph text ('Drag to rotate, scroll to zoom · loads a small 3D library on first use') is IDENTICAL on every real instance checked (5 so far) — static template markup, not a field.

btnId.description: Exact id of the toggle button — engine.js wires this up.

wrapId.description: Exact id of the hidden wrap div the 3D library mounts into.

hintId.description:
Optional — exact id of the hint

, when the real source gives it one.

btnLabel.description: The button's exact visible text INCLUDING the 🧊 emoji prefix, e.g. '🧊 View u × v in 3D' — real per-instance copy, not derived from the explorer title.

btnStyle.description: Optional inline style on the button, e.g. 'margin-top:0' — real per-instance CSS, present when the button is the ex-canvas's first child.

dataPanel.description: The 'View as data (non-visual equivalent)' accessible fallback — a real, deliberate accessibility feature (see project a11y-sweep history), not optional polish.

btnId.description: Exact id of the toggle button.

panelId.description: Exact id of the hidden panel — engine.js toggles its 'hidden' attribute.

descId.description:
Exact id of the

engine.js fills with a live description.

rowsId.description: Exact id of the <tbody> engine.js fills with live rows.

controls.description: Sliders. Empty/absent if the explorer has none.

valueDisplayId.description: Exact id of the <span> engine.js live-updates with the current value.

label.description: May contain simple inline HTML, e.g. 'Part a =' — matches source.

readouts.description: Live-updating readout rows below the controls. Empty/absent if the explorer has none.

id.description: Exact id of the <span class="v"> engine.js live-updates.

colorClass.description: Optional CSS color class on the row, e.g. 'indigo'/'amber' — matches source exactly, purely presentational.

value.description: The span's real initial text before any slider is touched — a WP23 audit found explorer.njk had hardcoded every readout to a literal em-dash placeholder, which happened to match qudrat's/tahsili's real source but silently discarded real precomputed defaults on act/act2/appc/apstats/apbc/est/est2/precalc (e.g. apstats' apsMean really starts at '31.67', not '—') — live and wrong on every one of those already-shipped pages. Copy the real source text verbatim, don't compute it.

note.description: Optional small note callout below the controls.

style.description:
def=definition, thm=theorem/rule, note=informational, warn=practice problem or caution, pf=proof, example=worked example (renders in the site's
wrapper), example-card=a worked example rendered in the smaller
stat-card wrapper instead (a real, if less common, pattern — e.g. qudrat ch.6/ch.8's extra worked examples), example-grid=a worked example rendered in
, a bold 'Worked Example · {label}' title line followed by raw-HTML

paragraphs (problem+solution run together, not split) — found in ibsl/ibhl/calculus, distinct from the plain 'example' style's label shape, tip=study-strategy tip. Maps to a template-owned CSS class — content authors pick a semantic style, not a class name.

label.description: Optional heading line, e.g. 'Definition — Antiderivative' or 'What to expect'. For example-grid, this is just the short title after 'Worked Example · ' (that prefix is static template markup, not part of the field).

body.description: Main prose. LaTeX allowed (\( \) inline, \[ \] display).

copyLatex.description: Optional: if this callout has a 'Copy LaTeX' button (rare — 7 instances sitewide as of WP6), the LaTeX string it copies. Math notation, not translated.

subtitle.en: Quantitative reasoning for Qiyas's General Aptitude Test

body.en: The General Aptitude Test (GAT — القدرات العامة, "Qudrat") is administered by Qiyas. Alongside a verbal section it has a quantitative section that measures reasoning with numbers rather than memorised content.
body.ar: يُدار اختبار القدرات العامة (GAT) من قِبل المركز الوطني للقياس ("قياس"). إلى جانب القسم اللفظي، يضم الاختبار قسمًا كمّيًا يقيس التفكير المنطقي بالأرقام بدلاً من المحتوى المحفوظ.

body.en: Questions are multiple choice and are answered without a calculator, so speed and clean mental methods matter as much as the mathematics.
Estimate before computing; keep fractions instead of converting to decimals where possible.
A student answers 36 out of 45 questions correctly. What percentage is that? <details><summary>Show solution</summary>80%.</details>
